<!-- pr-reviewer: 204e7c003441fd5a8c335764ee8093e9bc0714b4 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.** This is the first review of this PR. I read the full diff. I found no blocker.

Tier: this is not a SAFETY-tier change. The diff changes test support and tests in `camcraft-ui` only. It does not change posted G-code, a gouge or collision check, stock simulation or geometry. It does not change a UI page, so screenshots are not necessary.

## What looks good

- The PR does each item of "Done when" in #3605. The two trace binaries take one shared device through `headless_gpu::test_gpu`. The three ignored lib tests take `gpu_guard()` as their first statement.
- One lock has one home (`crates/ui/src/headless_gpu.rs`). The lib tests, the shared device and the integration binaries take the same lock.
- The `TestGpu` field order drops the two `Arc`s before the guard. Each test keeps the `TestGpu` value alive to the end of its scope. `both_eyes` in `trace_parity.rs` holds it for the full function.
- I checked the lock order. Each test that takes the two locks takes `gpu_guard()` first and `snapshot_guard()` second. No test takes them in the opposite order, so there is no deadlock between the two locks.
- `gpu_guard` is now library code. The PR removed the `assert_eq!` from it, and the pins read `gpu_holders()` instead. This obeys the Prime Directive (no panic outside tests). The poisoned lock is recovered, not unwrapped.
- The source-scan pins make a regression visible: a new per-test device in a trace binary, or a GPU test without the guard, fails a lib test.
- The decision file `docs/decisions/3605-gpu-test-device-lock.md` has the correct format: decided, why, dropped, cost to change.
- The body has the `Changelog:` line, the "Goldens moved" section and `Fixes #3605`. The commit subject is conventional and its body ends with `Fixes #3605`.

## Results (locally, macOS, Metal)

The PR head is on the current `upstream/main` (`83e5e8a37`). The trial merge gave "Already up to date", so the tested tree is the PR head `204e7c003`.

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` | 13 steps, 0 failed |
| ui build (`--no-run`) | ok |
| ui suites: lib | 1596 passed, 0 failed, 8 ignored |
| ui suites: trace_composite | 5 passed, 0 failed |
| ui suites: trace_parity | 5 passed, 0 failed |
| ui suites: boundary, boundary_picks, catalog_render, contour_dxf_sketch, sinker_setup, tap_hand, theme_example, theme_files, waterjet_tool | each ok |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |
| `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main --dry-run` | 0 steps: the diff reaches no heavy lane |

Extra suites run: none. The diff changes no file under `testdata/`, no fixture or golden directory, and no import code. It changes no post, operation, motion or catalog file, so `example_catalog` and the golden suites are not reached. No recorded program (`*.nc`, `*.cl`, `examples/catalog/**`) changed. No snapshot PNG changed.

## Mutations that I ran again

I ran `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib gpu_test_lock` for each mutation. I restored the tree after each one.

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| Lock removed (`gpu_guard` locks a new mutex for each call) | RED: `devices_asked_from_many_threads_are_one_device_used_one_at_a_time`, `the_lock_lets_one_holder_in_at_a_time` and `a_panic_with_the_lock_held_does_not_block_the_next_test` FAILED |
| Old call sites (`tests/trace_composite.rs` and `view_pass.rs` from `upstream/main`) | RED: `the_trace_binaries_share_one_locked_device` FAILED (`tests/trace_composite.rs: takes the shared device through test_gpu`). `every_gpu_test_takes_the_lock` FAILED (`view_pass.rs: ... must start with let _gpu = gpu_guard(); or take test_gpu`) |
| Restored tree | GREEN: 5 passed, 0 failed |

These results agree with the PR body.

## Requested before merge

None.

## Not exercised

- I did not run on Windows. The crash of #3605 (`0xC0000005`) occurs only on the hybrid-GPU Windows laptop. This review proves that the lock and the shared device work and that the pins hold. It does not prove that the crash is gone on that machine. The PR body says the same. The merging session must run `trace_composite`, `trace_parity` and the ui lib tests on that machine.
- I did not run the three ignored evidence renderers. They write PNGs and need opt-in environment variables. I read their first statements and the lock order only.

## Optional, non-blocking

1. `crates/ui/src/headless_gpu.rs:85` - on a machine with no adapter, `test_gpu` prints the SKIP line for each call. `device_for_test` prints one more SKIP line on the first call. The output is loud but correct.
2. `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/guide_images.rs` - the file had 408 lines and now has 409. It was above the 400-line limit before this PR. A split can go into a later PR.
3. `crates/ui/src/headless_gpu.rs:53` - `gpu_guard`, `gpu_holders` and `test_gpu` are public items of the shipped library, as `device_for_test` is. The integration binaries need them. No change is necessary.
4. The pixel-snapshot tests (`egui_shell_snapshot` and the others with `snapshot_guard()` only) render through the kittest renderer and take no `gpu_guard()`. They run only with `--ignored` in the release tier. #3605 does not name them. If the release tier shows the same crash on Windows, file a follow-up issue (`P7`).

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
Ready for merge from the merge loop: collaborator review 204e7c003 at head 204e7c003441fd5a8c335764ee8093e9bc0714b4.

Windows verification on the hybrid-GPU box (Windows 11, Intel Arc 140T and NVIDIA RTX 5050 Laptop), head `204e7c003`, in a separate worktree:

- `trace_composite` and `trace_parity`: 3 rounds each, with the default thread count. All rounds passed: 5 of 5 tests in each binary, 0 failed. On `main`, the same box crashed these suites with `0xC0000005` in some runs.
- `camcraft-ui` lib tests with `--test-threads=12` (#3379): 1597 passed, 0 failed, 8 ignored. There was no access violation.

The Windows check of this PR is complete. One clean run of the lib tests does not prove that #3379 is closed, because that crash was intermittent. The post-merge Windows checks will show it.
